title: Cold open
text: [excited] A guy is streaming live from the trunk of a moving car, and fifty-three thousand people are watching him outrun the cops. Lucia pulls a gun on the street, and the whole street backs away. A car flips, and the entire underside is there. [curious] None of that is from a trailer. It's the Extended Look. It's just the world doing its thing. [excited] Rockstar has shown us three GTA 6 videos, and hidden inside them is a new rulebook for open-world games. [mischievously] So here are seven reasons every open world after GTA 6 will have to play by it.

title: The world reacts to you
text: [curious] Reason one. The people. In most open worlds, a crowd has two settings: ignore you, or run screaming. Watch what GTA 6 does instead. [excited] Lucia pulls a gun on the street, and the people around her notice, back off, and she hides it behind her back. Inside the jewelry store, a customer tries to be a hero and grabs her weapon. And the moment the guard realizes he's outnumbered, he gives up. [whispers] Even a guy in a hallway shifts his hips so you don't bump into him. [curious] That's not a crowd. That's a city that watches you back.

title: It doesn't wait for you
text: [excited] Reason two. The world doesn't wait for you. In the Extended Look, a guy is livestreaming from the open trunk of a moving car. Fifty-three thousand viewers. A live chat scrolling in real time. And the cops are right behind him. [curious] Back at Lucia's place, a nature show is playing on the TV, and nobody's watching it. And a whole stretch of Trailer One is cut like a social feed: short clips, captions, usernames. [mischievously] Most open worlds pause the moment you look away. This one looks like it keeps posting.

title: Physics tells the story
text: [curious] Reason three. Physics. Jason drops into the driver's seat, and the whole car sinks and rocks on its suspension. He starts it, and a puff of white smoke hangs behind the exhaust. [excited] Lucia fires a shotgun, it kicks in her hands, and the spent shell hits the floor. In the raid, every shot rips plaster off the walls, and the dust just hangs there. [whispers] And when a police truck flips in the chase, the entire underside is modelled. [curious] None of this is needed to play the game. All of it tells you where you are, and what you're holding.

title: The downtime is the game
text: [curious] Reason four. The boring parts are playable. Every open world has a safehouse you never use. Now look at Lucia's apartment. Sticky notes on the fridge telling her to stay strong. She tries outfit after outfit while Jason waits, and there's an actual button prompt to tell her to hurry. [mischievously] He raids her fridge instead, and yes, the light inside comes on. [excited] Then they head to a rooftop bar called Effluvia, and walk in holding hands. [curious] That's not a safehouse menu. That's a life, and the game is asking you to live it.

title: Cops you outthink
text: [curious] Reason five. Getting away is a game of its own. After the jewelry store, Lucia doesn't run to a car. She sprints across the street and jumps on the back of a motorbike. [excited] Look at the wanted stars in the corner. Some of them are hollow. It seems to mean the cops know a crime happened, but not who did it yet. That's a theory... but it changes everything about how you escape. [whispers] Later, Jason and Lucia sit in a dark garage while a cop car rolls right past. [curious] In most games you outrun the police. Here, you outthink them.

title: A state, not a city
text: [excited] Reason six. The scale. Lucia runs off a rooftop, and below her is all of Vice City: canals, bridges, marinas, every block built for real. [curious] But Rockstar's own site says this is the whole state of Leonida. The Keys, where Jason lives on stilts. Grassrivers. Port Gellhorn. A mountain called Mount Kalaga. [mischievously] In the Extended Look alone we go from dirt bikes in the backcountry, to a private jet on a runway, to a party on top of a high-rise. [curious] Other open worlds give you a map. This one gives you somewhere to go.

title: Story and game are one thing
text: [curious] Reason seven. The big one. There's no line between the story and the game. A date on a rooftop turns into an offer over a cigarette. Deliver a car. Simple. [sarcastic] It is never simple. [excited] A stranger climbs into the back seat, the masks go on, a gun comes out, and now it's a chase. Then a phone lights up on the twenty-sixth floor. Guys everywhere. Ten-plus guys, automatic weapons. And the biggest gunfight Rockstar has shown starts right there. [mischievously] No mission title, no loading screen, none that Rockstar has shown. Just one night that keeps getting worse.

title: Here's why
text: [excited] So that's why. A world that reacts to you. A world that keeps running without you. Physics that tell a story. Downtime you actually play. Cops you outthink. A whole state to get lost in. And a story with no seams. [curious] Most open worlds treat those as separate features. GTA 6 treats them as one thing. That's the change. [mischievously] So which one do you think other studios copy first? Tell me in the comments. GTA 6 lands November nineteenth.
